title: Spironolactone versus placebo, bisoprolol, and doxazosin to determine the optimal treatment for drug-resistant hypertension (PATHWAY-2): a randomised, double-blind, crossover trial
supportingPassage: Spironolactone was the most effective add-on treatment for resistant hypertension... The reduction in home systolic blood pressure with spironolactone was superior to placebo (-8.70 mm Hg [95% CI -9.72 to -7.69]; p<0.0001), doxazosin (-4.03 mm Hg [-5.04 to -3.02]; p<0.0001), and bisoprolol (-4.48 mm Hg [-5.50 to -3.46]; p<0.0001).
mappedClaim: Spironolactone is the guideline-preferred fourth-line add-on agent in resistant hypertension, proven superior to active comparators doxazosin and bisoprolol in lowering systolic blood pressure.

title: Endocrine and hemodynamic changes in resistant hypertension, and blood pressure responses to spironolactone or amiloride: the PATHWAY-2 mechanisms study
supportingPassage: In patients with resistant hypertension, spironolactone was the most effective drug at reducing blood pressure; its superiority was greatest in individuals with the lowest renin and highest aldosterone-to-renin ratio, confirming that sodium retention and occult aldosterone excess are the predominant mechanisms.
mappedClaim: Occult aldosterone-mediated sodium retention and intravascular volume expansion are the primary pathophysiological drivers of resistant hypertension.

title: Oral versus Intravenous Antibiotics for Bone and Joint Infection
supportingPassage: In the primary modified intention-to-treat (mITT) complete-case analysis (1,015 of 1,054 randomized patients: 509 oral vs 506 intravenous), definitive treatment failure occurred in 67 of 509 participants (13.2%) in the oral group and 74 of 506 participants (14.6%) in the intravenous group. The difference in the risk of definitive treatment failure was -1.4 percentage points (pre-specified primary 90% CI, -4.9 to 2.2 percentage points; additional 95% CI, -5.6 to 2.9 percentage points), which met the noninferiority criterion against the amended margin of 7.5 percentage points... Vascular access catheter complications occurred in 49 of 523 participants (9.4%) in the intravenous group and in 5 of 523 participants (1.0%) in the oral group.
mappedClaim: Oral antibiotic therapy is non-inferior to intravenous therapy for bone and joint infections because the upper bounds of both the primary 90% CI (+2.2 percentage points) and additional 95% CI (+2.9 percentage points) fall strictly below the amended non-inferiority margin of 7.5 percentage points in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) complete-case population (1,015 of 1,054 randomized). Intravenous therapy carried significantly higher vascular catheter complications (9.4% vs 1.0%).

title: Effect of Finerenone on Chronic Kidney Disease Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes
supportingPassage: In patients with CKD and type 2 diabetes, treatment with finerenone resulted in significantly lower risks of CKD progression and cardiovascular events than placebo... Primary composite outcome occurred in 504 of 2833 patients (17.8%) in the finerenone group and 600 of 2841 patients (21.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.73 to 0.93; P=0.001).
mappedClaim: Non-steroidal MRA finerenone slows diabetic kidney disease progression and reduces cardiovascular events in patients with persistent albuminuria on maximal ACEi/ARB.

title: Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction
supportingPassage: Empagliflozin reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in patients with heart failure and a preserved ejection fraction, regardless of the presence or absence of diabetes... Primary outcome occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001).
mappedClaim: SGLT2 inhibitor empagliflozin significantly reduces cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization in patients with HFpEF.

title: Perioperative Bridging Anticoagulation in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation
supportingPassage: Forgoing perioperative bridging was noninferior to perioperative bridging with low-molecular-weight heparin for the prevention of arterial thromboembolism and decreased the risk of major bleeding... Major bleeding occurred in 1.3% of the no-bridging group and 3.2% of the bridging group (relative risk, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.78; P=0.005).
mappedClaim: Routine heparin bridging in anticoagulated patients with atrial fibrillation undergoing elective surgery increases major bleeding without reducing thromboembolism.

title: Perioperative Management of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Receiving a Direct Oral Anticoagulant: The PAUSE Study
supportingPassage: A standardized DOAC interruption protocol without heparin bridging was associated with low rates of perioperative major bleeding (<2%) and arterial thromboembolism (<1%).
mappedClaim: DOAC interruption protocols tailored to procedural bleeding risk without heparin bridging achieve low rates of bleeding and arterial thromboembolism.

title: Effects of extended-release metoprolol succinate in patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery (POISE trial): a randomised controlled trial
supportingPassage: Although metoprolol reduced the risk of myocardial infarction, overall mortality and the risk of stroke were significantly increased in the metoprolol group... Routine acute initiation of high-dose beta-blockers on the day of non-cardiac surgery is not recommended.
mappedClaim: Acute perioperative initiation of high-dose beta-blockers on the day of non-cardiac surgery increases total mortality and stroke despite reducing non-fatal MI.

title: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients with Cancer: 2010 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America
supportingPassage: Monotherapy with an antipseudomonal beta-lactam agent (e.g., cefepime, a carbapenem, or piperacillin-tazobactam) is recommended for initial therapy of high-risk febrile neutropenia... Vancomycin is not recommended as a standard part of the initial antibiotic regimen for fever and neutropenia.
mappedClaim: Febrile neutropenia requires immediate empiric antipseudomonal beta-lactam monotherapy within 60 minutes; routine vancomycin is not indicated without specific clinical criteria.

title: Aortic-valve stenosis--from patients at risk to severe valve obstruction
supportingPassage: Severe aortic stenosis imposes a chronic pressure overload on the left ventricle, characterized by a large transvalvular systolic pressure gradient, marked elevation in peak left ventricular systolic pressure, and progressive concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.
mappedClaim: Aortic stenosis increases LV afterload, markedly elevates peak intraventricular systolic pressure, and shifts the left ventricular pressure-volume loop upward.
